title: Autonomous Claude development supervisor (issue #44): telemetry, lifecycle, handoff, routing, Resolve discovery, GitHub log, Orbit, CLI, docs

lanes.title: Telemetry and evidence model: sessions, context pressure, usage signals (issue #44 part A)
acceptance_criteria: evidence.py: a small Evidence model with a source label (OBSERVED, REPORTED, INFERRED, UNAVAILABLE), timestamp, staleness check and helpers; every telemetry value carries a label and never an exact number the source does not expose

telemetry.py reads the Claude Code per-process session files (pid, sessionId, cwd, status busy/idle, name, startedAt, messaging socket path) from a configurable directory, tolerates missing/corrupt files and dead pids (liveness by pid probe, injectable), and reports staleness

telemetry.py computes per-session context pressure from the JSONL transcript by reading only the last assistant usage record (input + cache_read + cache_creation tokens, model id), with a configurable per-model context window table and thresholds (warn, compact, replace) as configuration with documented defaults; unknown model window gives UNAVAILABLE pressure, never a guess; tail read so large transcripts are not loaded whole; no transcript text is ever returned

Account usage and reset windows: a pluggable provider interface plus a statusline-JSON ingestor; with no source it returns UNAVAILABLE with the reason; the module documentation states plainly that nothing here is an account-usage reading unless a provider supplies it
A single snapshot function returns a JSON-serialisable dict (schema_version, generated_at, sessions[], each with the labelled fields) used later by the supervisor and Orbit

At least 40 offline tests with synthetic session files and synthetic transcripts (corrupt lines, huge line, missing usage, multiple models, dead pid, threshold edges); one real-machine OBSERVED run reported as numbers only

Synthetic data only: no real footage, no network in unit tests (a test patches socket creation to fail where a transport is involved), no secrets/tokens/keys printed, stored or committed, no absolute user paths in tracked files

Any evidence from the real machine (live observation) is summarised as numbers and identifiers only, never user prompts, transcript text or file contents; stated as OBSERVED with the exact command; anything not observed is labelled NOT TESTED
Nothing is described as VERIFIED without command output; the lane report separates implemented, tested, reported, proposed and open items

lanes.title: Supervisor state store and worker lifecycle: spawn, assign, monitor, restart, stop (issue #44 part B)
acceptance_criteria: state_store.py: a crash-safe machine-local store (atomic write, schema_version, fsync and rename, backup of the previous file, corruption detected and recovered from the backup, append-only JSON-lines event log) in a configurable directory that defaults OUTSIDE the repository; refuses a directory inside the repo working tree; no secrets ever written (scrub on write)

workers.py: a Worker record (id, role, task_id, branch, worktree, owner stream, provider/model identity, status, pid, session id, started and last-heartbeat, restart count, last result reference) and a registry that survives process restarts

lifecycle.py: spawn, assign, monitor, collect, restart and stop through an injected ProcessLauncher protocol (a fake launcher in tests; a real launcher that runs the claude CLI in print/stream-json mode with an explicit --model, --session-id and a task prompt file, argument lists only, no shell string interpolation, bounded runtime); heartbeat and stale detection; bounded restarts with backoff and a hard stop after N identical failures recorded as a blocker; graceful stop; duplicate-worker prevention for the same task/worktree; the worktree and branch must exist (injected checker) before a worker is assigned
Result collection: a worker result is stored as REPORTED until an injected verifier marks it VERIFIED or REJECTED; contradictory reports from two workers on one task are detected and flagged
Recovery: a fresh supervisor process reloads the registry, reconciles with live pids, marks vanished workers LOST and produces a recovery plan without relaunching anything automatically
At least 50 offline tests (fake launcher, fake clock, corruption, crash mid-write, restart storms, duplicate assignment, contradiction detection)

lanes.title: Safe handoff, compaction and session replacement (issue #44 part C)
acceptance_criteria: handoff.py: a handoff builder that captures objective, decisions, current plan, task graph, worker identities and status, branches/worktrees, latest commits and PRs, tests and evidence with labels, blockers, next actions and resource state (context and usage signals with their labels); written as machine-readable JSON plus a human Markdown file in the machine-local state store, with a content hash; a VERIFY step re-reads the files, validates the schema, checks that every referenced branch/worktree/commit/PR exists through injected checkers, and returns NOT_SAFE with reasons when anything is missing; contains no secrets or transcript text

compaction.py: a policy that, given context pressure from the L1 telemetry (merge origin/wave/w03-dev-supervisor to use it) and configurable thresholds, decides NONE / WARN / COMPACT / REPLACE with a recorded reason; compaction is only requested when the session is idle and a handoff has just been verified; never claims exact usage when the signal is UNAVAILABLE; a compaction event is recorded through the state store event log

replacement.py: the replace-a-session procedure: verify handoff, mark the old session retiring, launch a fresh Main or worker through the L2 launcher protocol with a prompt that points to the verified handoff, wait for the new session's first heartbeat, then retire the old; if the handoff is not verified the old session is never cleared; the module and its result state that a fresh session does NOT replenish account usage; bounded retries and rollback (the old session stays authoritative until the new one is confirmed)
At least 40 offline tests (missing branch, corrupt handoff, hash mismatch, threshold edges, retiring and rollback, never-clear-without-verified-handoff, repeated failure stops)

lanes.title: Provider/model routing and OmniRoute benchmarking (issue #44 part D)
acceptance_criteria: omniroute.py: a client over an injected HTTP transport for the local OmniRoute (base URL from configuration or env; the API key is read from the environment or the machine-local OmniRoute env file ONLY at call time, never logged, never stored, never in exceptions); lists models, sends a small benchmark prompt, records latency, status, token counts if returned and error class; localhost-only by default and refuses non-local base URLs unless explicitly allowed

routing.py: a task-profile scheduler: input is criticality, complexity class, estimated context size, deadline, concurrency, current context pressure and quota signals (each possibly UNAVAILABLE); output is a ranked decision with reasons (strongest Claude model for architecture, integration and high criticality; OmniRoute Gemini/Groq routes for routine, mechanical, search and repetitive work; escalation to Claude on validation failure or repeated failure; never a paid API route unless a configuration flag explicitly authorises it, default off); deterministic and fully explained; no fixed percentage split

A benchmark harness runs a fixed set of small synthetic tasks (code transform, JSON extraction, summarise, a tool-use style instruction, a refusal-safe task) against each reachable OmniRoute route, scores them with deterministic checkers (not an LLM judge), records pass rate, latency and failure class, and writes a results JSON containing no secrets

LIVE verification: run the harness against the local OmniRoute (the Coordinator started it on port 20128; if it is down start it with `omniroute serve --daemon --no-open`); report which Gemini/Groq routes answer, pass rates and latencies, which fail and why; write the factual results into OMNIROUTE_BENCHMARK.md labelled OBSERVED with date and commands; do not print or store any key, do not look for billing, do not configure paid providers
At least 40 offline tests; routing decisions covered for every branch including all-UNAVAILABLE signals and the paid-route-off default

lanes.title: Resolve project discovery and bridge bootstrap, read-only (issue #44 part E)
acceptance_criteria: INVESTIGATE first and write the findings into RESOLVE_BOOTSTRAP.md (OBSERVED versus inferred): why an agent could launch DaVinci Resolve Free 21.0.4.5 yet not identify the intended project or start the in-app bridge; read-only inspection only (process list, the listening bridge port 49632 on 127.0.0.1, .mcp.json.example, the davinci-resolve MCP read tools, local Resolve project metadata); you must NOT open, create, rename, save, import into or modify any project or timeline and must not click in Resolve; if a read needs the bridge and it is unavailable, document exactly what the user must do

resolve_discovery.py: a pure, injectable discovery module: is Resolve running (process check), is the bridge listening (TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 only), can the MCP answer a read-only call, current project name and stable identity (unique id where the API exposes one, else name plus database plus folder), current timeline name, project list; every field labelled OBSERVED or UNAVAILABLE; no guessing by name: it accepts a machine-local config of the expected project identity and reports MATCH, MISMATCH, UNCONFIGURED or UNAVAILABLE, and refuses to proceed on MISMATCH

A small CLI entry (`python -B -m dev_supervisor.resolve_discovery`) prints the report as JSON, exit code non-zero on MISMATCH or UNAVAILABLE; it never performs a project mutation; bridge start is documented, and launched only on an explicit flag and only as far as it can be done without touching a project; otherwise it prints the exact manual fallback

The real active project on this machine is DISCOVERED read-only and recorded (name, identity if available, timeline) in the lane report as OBSERVED; never written to a tracked file if it contains a personal path or a name not already public in the repository

At least 30 offline tests with a fake process list, fake socket and fake MCP transport (MISMATCH, UNCONFIGURED, bridge down, Resolve closed, timeouts); coordination note: T-RSV-002 owns the resolve_executor package and the exclusive 'resolve' resource; this lane is read-only and does not touch that package

lanes.title: Automatic GitHub progress reporting: durable event log (issue #44 part 5)
acceptance_criteria: github_log.py: an event model (task_started, step_done, decision, test_run, failure, retry, provider_change, handoff, compaction, blocker, pr_opened) with evidence references and a source label; renders a concise Markdown comment; every event is scrubbed (tokens, key/value secrets, absolute user paths, long opaque strings) before it leaves the process

Posting goes through an injected Runner protocol wrapping the gh CLI with argument lists (never shell strings): issue comment, issue create (sub-task), issue close; a real runner is provided but all tests use a fake; rate limiting and batching, bounded retries with backoff, an offline spool file (machine-local, atomic) so an event is never lost when GitHub or the network is down, and an idempotent flush (an event id marker prevents duplicate comments)
Visibility safety: the repository is PUBLIC; the logger refuses to post content flagged as sensitive (secret pattern, transcript text marker, personal path) and records the refusal locally instead
A helper creates a sub-task issue from a task record (id, owner, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria, branch/worktree) with a back-reference to the parent issue number
At least 40 offline tests (fake gh runner, outage plus spool plus flush, duplicate prevention, scrubbing, refusal)

acceptance_criteria: snapshot.py builds one read-only JSON for Orbit from the L1 telemetry and the L2 registry (Main, workers, tasks, model/provider, context pressure with labels, account usage only when OBSERVED, branch/PR, last durable GitHub checkpoint, blockers, failures, retries, next actions); each value says whether it is live or cached and its age; stale and offline are first-class states

lanes.title: Supervisor CLI and one-command launch of Main (issue #44 integration)
acceptance_criteria: config.py: machine-local configuration (state directory outside the repo, thresholds, model table, OmniRoute base URL, GitHub repo and issue, paid-route flag default off) loaded from a machine-local file; a documented example is committed as a template with placeholders only

cli.py and __main__.py: `python -B -m dev_supervisor` with subcommands start (launch Main under the supervisor), status, workers, assign, handoff, compact-check, replace, report (flush the GitHub log), snapshot, route (explain a routing decision), doctor (check claude CLI, git, gh, OmniRoute, Resolve discovery, state dir, repo clean); each is non-destructive by default and exits non-zero on a failed check; the documented single launch command starts Main and the supervisor loop

launch.py: starts Main as a claude CLI session with the verified handoff and operating instructions as an appended prompt file, in the repository root, with a selectable profile that only passes flags (model, permission mode as configured) and NEVER reads, copies or modifies pro.ps1, backup.ps1 or .mcp.json; the Claude Pro versus OmniRoute choice is made by which local launcher the user runs and is documented, not automated by editing those launchers; the dangerous-permissions flag is only passed when the machine-local config explicitly enables it

lanes.title: Development operating system documentation and doc reconciliation (issue #44 part G)
acceptance_criteria: DEVELOPMENT_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md (project-independent, placeholders instead of machine values): how Main controls the operation; how specialist agents communicate (Claude Code messaging, GitHub as the durable log); the Python supervisor, session/context rotation and recovery; GitHub task/step/event logging, branches, worktrees, PRs and integration; Orbit and what it observes; Claude Pro versus OmniRoute (free Gemini/Groq, no paid API assumed) with quota realities and the statement that a fresh session does not replenish usage; Windows/VS Code setup and machine-local configuration; how to onboard a new repository; how Main proposes ideas, evaluates feasibility and trade-offs and asks essential questions before a major build; and the distinction between reusable development infrastructure and Creator Studio's video-production agents

Every capability in the document is labelled with its real status (IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, OBSERVED, REPORTED, PROPOSED, NOT TESTED) taken from the lane reports and the merged code on the wave branch, with nothing promoted beyond its evidence
